sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: This species shares with I. phalloides a phallus-shaped caecum in both the soldier and the worker: the caecum sends forward a finger-like projection whose distal end may be inflated or cap-like, coronate, and on this basis both differ from all other species of the genus; the soldiers of the two are similar in morphology, differing only slightly in mandibular curvature; but their ecology differs, this species occurring in mainland evergreen forest and I. phalloides in forest galleries. The worker enteric valve architecture (EVA) is of the finitimus type; the workers are small within the genus and their head capsules average slightly wider than in I. phalloides. The soldier EVA is generally recognisable as the finitimus type, and its mandibles average longer than in I. phalloides: left mandible ventral length SMlL = 2.17–2.53 mm (1.99–2.36 mm in I. phalloides). Alate unknown. At present known only from forest environments in northern Republic of the Congo and Cameroon.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule on the pale side (Cf4–Cf5), grading from a darker frons to a paler posterior; antennae and labrum concolorous with the frons or slightly paler; mandibles dark (C7–C8), abruptly paler at the base (C5–C6) and concolorous with the frons; thorax and legs generally paler than the head capsule (C3–C4); abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents, the tergites sometimes with a pale yellow tinge. Head capsule with a few scattered setae; a dense tuft of hairs surrounds and covers the frontal gland pore; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); the labrum always with 3–6 large setae on each lateral lobe; pronotum and mesonotum with few setae, mainly on the margins. Fore coxa with 1–3 spines on the ridge and none (very rarely 1) on the ventral surface; trochanter with 2–8 spines; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, each tibia with a row of 8–15 spines. Abdominal tergites with the large setae mainly on the posterior margin; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward and often pigmented, together with smaller setae directed posteriorly. Soldier medium-sized within the genus. Head capsule distinctly sclerotized, distinctly longer than wide; in dorsal view the sides usually nearly parallel, distinctly narrowing in the posterior quarter, converging from the antennal sockets towards the mandible bases, the posterior margin regularly rounded or briefly straight in the middle; the upper margin concave; the angle between the projecting mandibles and the frons slightly obtuse; frons without or with only a weak anterior swelling. Gulamentum narrowing in the posterior half in ventral view, the anterior half widening at sharp angles or ear-like at the sides. Antennae 14.5–15 segmented. Labrum always deeply forked, wider than long, the sides harp-shaped; the lobes angular, their tips fine and semitransparent; the anterior margin concave. Mandibles sabre-like, distinctly shorter than the head, the inner margin smooth, each mandible with 1 distinct but very small marginal tooth near the molar area; the surface of both mandibles smooth and shining; the right mandible slightly more curved than the left. Pronotum saddle-shaped, 59%–64% of the head width, the anterior and posterior margins generally entire; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally, forming a more or less sharp ridge. Enteric valve inserted on the left side, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Caecum always fairly well developed, best seen in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, a typical finger-like projection extending forward, generally inflated distally or appearing cap-like. Primary cushions (PC) arranged with trigonal symmetry, the odd cushion 20%–25% longer than the even ones, the inflation marking the place where the setae become very dense distally (compare the worker EVA). Measurements: head dorsal concavity sagitta 0.02–0.07 mm, head length 2.71–3.12 mm, head width 1.84–2.13 mm, left mandible ventral length 2.17–2.53 mm, left mandible minor curvature 0.18–0.26 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale (C2–C3); proximal antennal segments pale (C2), the apical segment two shades darker (C4); thorax, tergites and legs pale (C1–C3); abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents. Head capsule and postclypeus with a few scattered erect setae; labrum with a few scattered stout setae; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); thoracic tergites with scattered setae. Fore coxa ridged, with 1 fine seta, 3–6 spines on the ridge and 1–2 ventrally; fore trochanter with 5–7 spines; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, and with a row of 6–15 spines. Abdominal tergites with scattered setae; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward and often pigmented, together with smaller setae directed posteriorly. Workers medium-sized on average within the genus. Head capsule weakly sclerotized (except the mandibles). Antennae 14.5 segmented (very rarely 14). Labrum domed. Left mandible with a well-developed apical tooth, sharp when unworn; 3 marginal teeth, the first well developed but blunt even when fresh, the second weak (expressed only as an undulating tooth margin, lost with wear), the third with a blunt tip; the proximal premolar not hidden by the molar prominence; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible with a well-developed apical tooth, sharp when fresh; 2 marginal teeth, the first well developed and sharp when fresh, the second smaller and blunt even when fresh; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum saddle-shaped, 66%–71% of the head width; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Enteric valve inserted on the left, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Primary cushions arranged in the finitimus type with trigonal symmetry: the downstream part of the odd cushion is broad, its bulbous inflation bearing denser shorter setae; supporting setae numerous, 18–33 on each side of the odd cushion; secondary cushions broad upstream, distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed. Caecum always well developed, best seen in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, finger-like, extending forward, often inflated distally or cap-like. Measurements: maximum head width 1.15–1.26 mm, distance from the left apical tooth to the first marginal tooth 0.16–0.20 mm, left mandible functional length 0.54–0.59 mm, mean length of primary cushions 1–6 0.53–0.61 mm, mean width 0.06–0.08 mm, mean length of secondary cushions 0.42–0.47 mm, mean width 0.19–0.24 mm, odd primary cushion elongation index WVPOdd-Elg = 6.76–10.2.

note: Adapted from the genus revision in Josens et al. (2025), original in English; the alate is not described in the original (imago unknown); measurements from Table 10 and the text of the original; distribution, hosts, DNA and figure numbers are not translated.
